messages:
sam: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a "credits stitching" pattern for the billing pipeline. TL;DR: attach a stable billing_id as early as practical and reconcile token attribution at a deterministic finalize step. Need to decide tradeoffs on where to dedupe and who owns the canonical mapping.

maria: I still lean early attachment. fewer edge cases for retries/duplicates and realtime dashboards become simpler.

kevin: main concern is streaming responses where tokens are flushed incrementally. If we attach on first packet we can mis-credit when a session switches model or route midstream.

sam: agreed. Two high level options:
  1) attach at request-finalize (post-facto stitched attribution) — simpler ingestion but more complex reconcile job
  2) incremental commits with `commit_seq` markers (commit at logical points) — more state in ingest, lower later complexity

jen: audit/legal requirement: we must keep an immutable raw event store for all inbound events plus a provenance hash. We can re-attribute later but keep the original blob.

maria: raw_events -> cold S3 + index on event_hash sounds good. But we need a low-latency summarized stream for billing exporters, can't always wait for finalize. Suggest dual-path: raw -> cold store; summary -> billing queue.

arjun: performance note: embedding the full `attribution` array in each event increases payload ~30-50%. At 10k rps that's a noticeable throughput/cost hit. Can we use compact encoding (proto) or pointers (`attribution_id`) instead of full structs?

liz: interface proposal to make ownership explicit: expose `meter.append(event)` for partial token chunks and `meter.finalize(request_id, final_meta)` which emits final stitched billing events. Ingest layer owns append semantics, billing service owns finalize semantics.

kevin: followup: who dedupes retries? we should make dedupe deterministic at ingest shard using `request_id` as idempotency key. Also need a strategy for out-of-order commit_seq.

maria: +1 on idempotency. Also we can't wait forever for late chunks — need a watermark. Default grace window idea: 60s, configurable per-customer.

sam: noted. Also need to handle super-late arrivals that should be audited but not change billing retrospectively. Maybe allow a "correction" passthrough that generates audit-only correction events.

jen: on audits — we'll require: immutable raw blob retention (90d hot, 7y cold), event_hash, and a signed provenance record for any finalized billing event. I'll draft the storage SLO and retention policy.

arjun: action item for perf: prototype compact attribution encoding and measure bytes/event and ingestion CPU. If we can shrink payload by 40% we gain a lot.

kevin: streaming commit_seq semantics to spec: treat `commit_seq` as monotonically increasing per request_id; ingest accepts out-of-order but buffers up to N sequences or time window, then emits partial commit events. I'll write RFC section.

maria: question: how do we handle multi-model requests (client fanout -> multiple models) for cost allocation? suggestion: attribution entries with `model`, `tokens`, `cost_basis` and a `primary` boolean for destination owner.

sam: good pattern. We'll also include a `provenance_id` field that points to raw blob for any stitched entry.

liz: small API suggestion to keep clients simple: allow `meter.append` to accept `final=false` and `meter.finalize` with `final=true`. Server returns `status: appended` or `status: finalized` and optionally `billing_id`. Keep the finalizer single RPC to make rollouts easier.

sam: action items (owners):
 - update RFC to add `meter.append` + `meter.finalize` + raw_event retention (owner: sam)
 - prototype compact attribution encoding + perf test (owner: arjun)
 - write audit storage SLO + retention doc (owner: jen)
 - spec streaming commit_seq behavior + buffer semantics (owner: kevin)
 - decide default grace window and per-customer override API (owner: maria + liz)

infra-bot: deploy: metering-staging v0.31 -> rolled to staging, smoke tests passed :rocket:

liz: let's do a 15m sync tomorrow to lock default grace window. :calendar:

sam: created followup PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/512 — please review :eyes:

maria: skimmed, left comments on compact encoding section.

kevin: added note about model-switch-mid-stream edge case in the PR.

jen: posted draft audit doc in drive: https://drive.google.com/xxx (internal only).

sam: thanks everyone — I'll fold comments into the RFC and ping for reviews. :+1:
